interest: Details Japan's transition to wartime exchange controls and the resulting freeze of 30 million yen in American funds.
overview: This file documents the evolution of Japan’s foreign exchange and monetary policies from December 1931 to September 1937, beginning with the reimposition of the gold export embargo and the subsequent depreciation of the yen. It traces government efforts to peg exchange rates, the enactment of the Foreign Exchange Control Law, and mounting economic strains driven by heavy capital investments in Manchukuo. Following the 1937 outbreak of the North China incident, the records detail emergency financial measures, drastic import licensing restrictions, administrative bottlenecks, and the freezing of approximately 30 million yen of American funds, culminating in U.S. State Department evaluations and diplomatic instructions to Ambassador Joseph C. Grew to monitor discrimination against American creditors.
